stimulus: Tone languages use pitch to tell apart words that would otherwise sound the same. To compare how such systems develop, field linguist Dana Okafor gathered recordings from three regions: Yorubaland, in southwestern Nigeria______ the highlands of northern Vietnam, where Hmong is spoken; and Oaxaca, Mexico, home to several Zapotec varieties.
explanation: This is a list of three regions, and the items already contain commas ("Yorubaland, in southwestern Nigeria"; "Oaxaca, Mexico"). Later in the sentence the items are separated by a semicolon ("spoken; and Oaxaca"). The blank falls between the first and second items, so it needs the same separator: a semicolon.

A.why: The comma before "in southwestern Nigeria" made another comma look natural here. You decided from the nearby words and didn't check the semicolon later in the list. Because the items contain their own commas, a comma at the blank makes it hard to tell where one region ends and the next begins.

C.why: The colon after "three regions" already introduces the list. A second colon in the middle of the list doesn't introduce anything; it just breaks the series at a point where it makes no sense.

D.why: With no punctuation, "Nigeria" runs straight into "the highlands," so two separate list items fuse into one. The list needs a separator here, and it has to match the semicolon used later.
